propositions: The gate matches config field names globally as bare attribute terminals rather than resolving reads to their owning dataclass, causing same-named fields on unrelated configs to satisfy each other and creating false negatives for inert fields with common names.

Fields like CodeHealthConfig.enabled passed the gate despite zero direct reads because the bare name 'enabled' appeared on unrelated configs (UiConfig.enabled, McpConfig.auth_enabled), while uniquely-named inert fields like CodeHealthConfig.analyzers correctly triggered the gate.

The fix must resolve each attribute read to its declaring dataclass through section names, annotations, local assignments, return types, and cross-module call-site binding, so a field is satisfied only by reads of its owner class.

Four fields are newly flagged by the corrected gate and must receive accurate # read-via: markers citing their real readers: McpConfig.readonly, McpConfig.allow_llm, McpConfig.allow_jira_sync, and JiraConfig.allow_insecure.

Test suites must be migrated from the defective bare-name contract to owner-resolution, including inverting test_unrelated_same_named_attribute_keeps_the_gate_quiet to expect the gate to fire on inert fields with reused names.
Any # read-via: marker naming a closed rebar ticket ID must be reported by the gate so expired exemptions surface instead of persisting silently.
